item.title: Brazil's imprisoned ex-president Jair Bolsonaro taken to hospital with 'severe abdominal pain'
item.description: Jair Bolsonaro has been hospitalized due to intense abdominal pain linked to his declining health condition. Concerned for his father’s well-being, Carlos Bolsonaro has voiced worries over the treatment and persistent psychological pressure. After sustaining multiple stab wounds, Bolsonaro is serving a lengthy prison sentence for alleged coup attempts. In a related note, his eldest son Flavio faced electoral defeat and subsequently relocated to the United States with his family.
item.dc:creator: Trisha Mahajan

item.title: 'Look at India', 'country of 2nd chances': 10 takeaways from Trump's White House presser
item.description: Donald Trump championed his administration's initiatives and signaled a willingness to partner with Democrats on key issues. He lauded the economic prospects of the Quad alliance, particularly India's remarkable growth figures. Discussing Iran, Trump called for clear and acceptable terms in any agreements. Supporting former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, he recommended enforcing a tax on offshore data centers.

item.title: Louisiana couple's $429,000 home defects case revived against property brokerage by appeals court
item.description: A couple in Louisiana filed a lawsuit against the sellers and brokerage after discovering defects post-purchase. They claimed that significant issues, such as a rotted air pipe and rodent remains, were concealed. The court ruled that the relationship between the agent and brokerage required further examination. While the jury dismissed some claims, questions about the agent's status remain unresolved.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: A Virginia woman who looks after 27 nest boxes near her home has helped 1,674 baby bluebirds take flight since 2006, checking every box each week from April to July and logging every single egg
item.description: Cathi Morrison has dedicated her efforts to monitoring 27 bluebird nesting boxes since 2006. She documents every nesting attempt, egg, and fledgling, contributing valuable data to conservation organizations. Morrison highlights the challenges young bluebirds face, including predators and extreme weather conditions. She emphasizes the importance of maintaining an environment that supports insect populations necessary for bluebird survival. Morrison encourages community involvement in supporting local bird populations and creating healthier ecosystems.

item.title: Platte County treasurer faces lawsuit over alleged $1.3 million bank transaction
item.description: Kimberlie Miller has initiated legal action against Treasurer Chris Kendall and Platte County following her dismissal. She asserts that her firing occurred after she flagged a suspicious transaction linked to a $1.3 million cheque directed to an unauthorized account. Miller's lawsuit encompasses various claims, including discrimination and wage discrepancies, with a hearing set for February 2027.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Kansas family harvesting crops 13 miles north of Syracuse filmed a rare piebald black bear with patchy light and dark fur, the first a state wildlife biologist says he has ever seen in Kansas.
item.description: A family in Kansas spotted a rare piebald black bear while harvesting crops in their field. The unusual bear had distinct patches of light and dark fur, surprising wildlife experts. Typically, black bears in the region are known to have cinnamon-colored fur. Wildlife biologists explained that young bears often disperse in search of food and territory.
item.dc:creator: TOI Lifestyle Desk

item.title: Australian data centre with Anthropic faces 595 objections over power, water, traffic and noise
item.description: Residents of Queensland are raising alarms over a proposed data centre that may significantly impact their community. Concerns have been voiced regarding heightened water usage, the strain on electricity supply, increased noise levels, and road infrastructure challenges. Zerra DC, the developer, is committed to engaging with locals and addressing their issues. The ambitious plan to establish one of Australia's largest computing facilities is now pending necessary planning and regulatory approvals.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Florida couple find 15-foot, 134-pound python during late-night dog walk
item.description: Late one night, while taking their dog for a stroll in Chase Preserve, Florida, a couple stumbled upon a massive Burmese python. Residents soon gathered, alarmed by the sight of the snake lurking in the bushes, prompting a call for assistance. A local trapper swiftly captured the hefty 134-pound female python in only three minutes.

item.title: Amazon communities have a complicated relationship with giant anacondas; a 2025 study explores why some people fear them while others live alongside them
item.description: Communities in the Lower Amazon have a multifaceted relationship with giant anacondas, dealing with folklore and livestock concerns. The presence of these snakes is often rooted in local myths, but practical encounters create conflicts. Killing anacondas frequently stems from protecting domestic animals rather than pure fear. Researchers indicate that the people's perceptions of the snakes have altered due to economic considerations.
item.dc:creator: TOI Lifestyle Desk

item.title: Denver detective accused of DUI, fleeing crash in city SUV; deputies stop, identify her at gunpoint
item.description: A Denver police detective has been charged with DUI and hit-and-run after allegedly crashing a city-provided SUV into a parked car in an Arapahoe County neighbourhood and fleeing. Deputies stopped the damaged vehicle at gunpoint after it travelled nearly a mile on three tyres and a rim. The detective later resigned from the department.

item.title: Sara Bareilles helps raise $1.8m for New York public radio at gala
item.description: Sara Bareilles graced the stage at a New York City gala, successfully raising over $1.8 million for New York Public Radio. The event gathered more than 500 attendees to emphasize the vital role of independent journalism and cultural initiatives. This yearly gala underscores the community's commitment to maintaining strong public broadcasting, with funds aimed at bolstering NYPR's diverse offerings, including news coverage and classical music shows.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: US postal inspector jailed for 40 months after stealing $340,000 from elderly scam victims
item.description: Scott Steven Kelley, a former US Postal Inspector, received a 40-month prison sentence for stealing money from elderly victims. He embezzled over $340,000 by intercepting postal packages meant for fraud victims. The money was used for personal expenses, including home improvements and family vacations. Federal authorities have worked to identify the victims and ensure restitution.
